headline: Daily market snapshot July 24 2026
summary: US equities head for weekly losses as AI capex fears from Alphabet and Tesla earnings trigger Magnificent Seven selloff of $797B; Brent crude eases to $98.82 after briefly topping $100 on Houthi attacks; gold holds near $4,028 and 10Y Treasury yields rise to 4.66%.

headline: Alphabet Q2 2026 revenue beats on cloud surge but stock sinks on $205B capex outlook
summary: Alphabet reported Q2 2026 revenue of $119.8B (+24% YoY, vs $116.9B est) and raised full-year capex guidance to $195-205B from $180-190B. Cloud revenue jumped 82% to $24.77B and cloud backlog swelled to $514B, but the massive capex hike sent shares down ~6%.

headline: Alphabet delivers Q2 beat with cloud revenue surging 82%, capex disappoints
summary: Alphabet's Google Cloud division posted 82% year-over-year revenue growth to $24.77B in Q2 2026, ahead of the $24.56B consensus. Cloud contract backlog reached $514B with roughly half expected to convert within 24 months, but the company's single-quarter capex hit $45B.

headline: Alphabet raises 2026 capex guidance to $195-205B; FCF turns negative for first time since IPO
summary: Alphabet hiked its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195-205B, a $15B increase at the midpoint, driven by accelerated data center and computing infrastructure for AI. The massive investment pushed Alphabet's free cash flow negative for the first time since its IPO.
key_facts: AI infrastructure and data center expansion cited
FCF turned negative for first time since IPO

headline: Tesla Q2 2026: revenue beats at $28.24B but adjusted EPS $0.33 misses $0.53 estimate
summary: Tesla reported Q2 2026 revenue of $28.24B (+26% YoY), beating the $25.55B consensus by 10.5%, but adjusted EPS of $0.33 fell well short of the $0.53 estimate. GAAP net income was $1.11B and free cash flow turned negative at -$1.1B on $5.8B quarterly capex.

headline: Tesla faces major selloff following Q2 earnings, stock drops 14.5% — largest decline since March 2025
summary: Tesla stock fell 14.5% on July 24, its largest single-day decline since March 2025, erasing approximately $214.5B in market capitalization. The selloff was driven by the Q2 EPS miss and investor concerns about AI and robotics spending trajectory amid negative free cash flow.

headline: Magnificent Seven loses $797 billion in market cap as AI skeptics dump tech stocks
summary: The Magnificent Seven tech stocks collectively shed $797B in market value on July 23 as investors reacted to escalating AI capex commitments from Alphabet and Tesla. The Magnificent Seven index fell 4.8%, its largest single-day drop since the April 2025 tariff tantrum.
key_facts: Largest single-day drop since April 2025 tariff tantrum
Industry AI capex on track for $700B+ in 2026
M7 forward FCF well below 2024 levels

headline: Trump imposes 10-12.5% tariffs on 60 economies using forced-labor rationale
summary: The US imposed tariffs of 10% or 12.5% on imports from its top 60 trading partners — covering 99.4% of American imports — effective July 24, the expiration date of the prior Section 122 stopgap. Countries deemed compliant with forced-labor bans face 10%; non-compliant face 12.5%.
key_facts: Covers top 60 US trade partners, 99.4% of imports
Countries affected include Australia, China, Singapore, South Korea
China, HK, Singapore, South Korea receive 12.5%

headline: Trade partners from Australia to Brazil reject Trump's 'arbitrary' forced-labor tariff rationale
summary: US trading partners globally condemned the forced-labor justification for Trump's new 10-12.5% tariffs as arbitrary and unfair, but most signaled they would continue negotiating rather than immediately retaliating, avoiding a near-term escalation.
key_facts: Australia, Brazil, South Korea, Singapore reject rationale
Most nations signal continued negotiation over retaliation
Tariffs replace Section 122 stopgap expiring July 24

headline: Brent tops $100 as Houthi attacks push oil rally into triple digits
summary: Brent crude futures closed above $100 per barrel on July 23 for the first time in months, rising ~7% to $100.69 as Iran-backed Houthi militants attacked Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, announcing a blockade of Saudi ports. WTI also surged ~6% to $92.19.
key_facts: Houthi militants attacked two Saudi oil tankers
Houthis declared blockade of Saudi ports
Oil futures up 13%+ on the week
Trump threatened to extend US strikes on Iran

headline: Brent eases to $98.82, WTI at $90.46 on July 24 as oil pulls back slightly from $100+ peak
summary: After surging above $100 on July 23, Brent crude pulled back 1.9% to $98.82 per barrel in early July 24 European trading as some profit-taking set in, while WTI retreated 1.9% to $90.46. Oil prices remain up more than 13% on the week.
key_facts: Houthi attacks ongoing in Red Sea

headline: Houthis attack Saudi oil tankers in Red Sea, declare blockade of Saudi ports
summary: Iran-backed Houthi militants claimed responsibility for attacking two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, framing the strikes as enforcement of a newly announced blockade of Saudi ports. The attacks drove Brent crude above $100 for the first time in months.
key_facts: Two Saudi tankers attacked in Red Sea
Houthis claimed blockade of Saudi ports
Trump threatened extended US strikes on Iran
Iran warned of retaliation against US-linked energy assets

headline: AT&T Q2 2026 beats: adj EPS $0.65 vs $0.59 est, 432K postpaid phone adds, broadband record
summary: AT&T reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.65 vs the $0.59 consensus, on revenue of $31.6B (+2.3% YoY). The company added 432K postpaid phone net subscribers vs 338.5K estimated and a combined 646K broadband net adds (367K fiber + 279K FWA — a record). Full-year guidance left intact.
key_facts: 432K postpaid phone net adds vs 338.5K est
FY guidance intact: adj EPS $2.25-2.35, FCF $18B+

headline: American Express Q2 2026 earnings beat; adj EPS $4.28, FY guidance $17.30-17.90
summary: American Express reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $4.28, topping the consensus estimate, with revenue of $18.91B. The company reiterated full-year EPS guidance of $17.30-17.90 per share. Stock dipped modestly after results as broader market headwinds weighed.
key_facts: Q2 reported July 24 before market open

headline: Verizon Q2 2026: revenue falls short of expectations, EPS in line
summary: Verizon reported Q2 2026 results before the July 24 open with revenue coming in below the ~$35.2B consensus expectation, while adjusted EPS landed roughly in line at approximately $1.28. Key focus areas included postpaid phone net adds acceleration from Q1's 55K and FWA broadband growth.
key_facts: Q1 postpaid adds were only 55K, first positive Q1 in 13 years

headline: NextEra Energy releases Q2 2026 results July 24; consensus EPS $1.10, revenue $8.15B
summary: NextEra Energy released its Q2 2026 financial results before market open on July 24. The consensus estimate called for EPS of approximately $1.10-1.11 (+5.7% YoY) on revenue of $8.15-8.17B (+21.9% YoY). NextEra has beaten earnings estimates in roughly 88% of quarters historically.
key_facts: Q2 results released July 24 before open
CEO John Ketchum, CFO Mike Dunne present webcast

headline: Markets see 34% chance Fed hikes rates at July 28-29 FOMC meeting
summary: Money markets assigned roughly 34% odds to a Federal Reserve rate hike at the July 28-29 FOMC meeting under Chair Kevin Warsh, with a 78% probability of at least one quarter-point increase by September. The July meeting will not include a Summary of Economic Projections, making it primarily a communication event.
key_facts: Chair Kevin Warsh press conference at 2:30 PM ET July 29

headline: 10-year Treasury yield rises to 4.659%, 2-year at 4.304% as Fed hike bets stay elevated
summary: The 10-year US Treasury yield climbed to 4.659%, up more than 3 basis points, as markets priced in elevated probability of Fed tightening. The 2-year yield rose 4 basis points to 4.304%, reflecting short-term rate hike expectations driven by persistent inflation above the 2% target.
key_facts: Oil price surge stoking inflation fears

headline: S&P Global US Flash Services PMI 55.2, Manufacturing 49.5 in July 2026
summary: S&P Global's July 2026 flash PMIs showed divergence: services PMI rose to 55.2 from 52.9, while manufacturing slipped to 49.5 (below the 50 expansion threshold). The US Composite PMI climbed to 54.6, consistent with annualized GDP growth of approximately 2.3%.

headline: Asian equities slapped down July 24; KOSPI triggers sidecar curbs on AI capex selloff
summary: Asian markets fell sharply on July 24 as the Magnificent Seven's $797B market cap loss rippled into the region. Japan's Nikkei 225 fell approximately 2.5%, and South Korea's KOSPI triggered sidecar trading curbs, with KOSDAQ halted after futures dropped more than 6%.
key_facts: Driven by Mag7 $797B selloff and AI capex fears
South Korea regulator advanced leveraged ETF margin requirements to July 31

headline: South Korea regulator advances leveraged ETF margin requirement to July 31 amid tech volatility
summary: South Korea's financial regulator moved up the start date for higher deposit requirements on retail trading of single-stock leveraged ETFs to July 31, requiring approximately 30 million won ($20,000) cash deposit. The rule targets speculative retail positions in Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix leveraged products, which have amplified market volatility.
key_facts: Targets Samsung and SK Hynix single-stock leveraged ETFs
Approved in late May; accelerated amid market volatility
KOSDAQ halted July 24 on -6% futures drop

headline: European stocks edge higher July 24 as US futures recover; DAX +0.5%, FTSE +0.1%
summary: European equities posted modest gains on July 24 as US stock index futures rebounded from Thursday's tech-driven rout. Germany's DAX rose 0.5%, France's CAC 40 gained 0.1%, the FTSE 100 added 0.1%, and the Stoxx Europe 600 climbed 0.2%. Brent crude eased 1.9% to $98.82.

headline: Gold at $4,028 defending $4,000 support as Brent $100+ and 80% Sep hike odds weigh
summary: Gold traded around $4,028 per ounce on July 24, extending a 2% decline from the prior session as surging oil prices reinforced tighter-Fed expectations, pressuring the non-yielding metal. Gold is defending the key $4,000 psychological floor, with September rate hike odds jumping to 78-80%.
key_facts: Oil surge stoking inflation, Fed tightening expectations

headline: Bitcoin near $64,680, Ethereum ~$1,933 as crypto prices mixed amid analyst debate
summary: Bitcoin was trading near $64,680 and Ethereum around $1,933 as of July 23-24, with crypto prices mixed amid analyst disagreement over whether the market had reached a bottom. Risk-off sentiment from tech's AI capex selloff weighed on digital assets alongside broader markets.
key_facts: Risk-off from Mag7 selloff weighs on digital assets

headline: AI infrastructure capex on track for $700B+ in 2026, a 70% YoY jump; M7 forward FCF under pressure
summary: Industry-wide capital expenditures tied to AI infrastructure are on pace to exceed $700B in 2026, representing a ~70% year-over-year jump. The spending surge has meaningfully compressed forward free cash flow for the Magnificent Seven, which now sit well below 2024 FCF levels on a 12-month forward basis.
key_facts: ~70% YoY increase in AI infrastructure spend

headline: Wolfe Research upgrades AT&T to Outperform from Peer Perform, raises target to $29
summary: Wolfe Research upgraded AT&T from Peer Perform to Outperform and assigned a $29 price target, citing the telecom's improving subscriber trajectory, strong Q2 broadband performance, and maintained dividend. The upgrade followed AT&T's Q2 earnings beat.
key_facts: Upgraded to Outperform from Peer Perform
AT&T Q2 432K postpaid adds, 646K broadband net adds

headline: Guggenheim initiates Tyler Technologies with Buy rating and $440 target
summary: Guggenheim initiated coverage of Tyler Technologies with a Buy rating and a $440 price target, highlighting the government software company's durable recurring revenue streams and strong execution in public-sector digital transformation contracts.

headline: KeryBanc upgrades Ameren to Overweight from Sector Weight, sets $122 target
summary: KeryBanc upgraded Ameren from Sector Weight to Overweight with a $122 price target, citing the utility's expanding renewable generation buildout and relatively defensive earnings profile amid elevated interest rates.
key_facts: Upgraded to Overweight from Sector Weight

headline: US existing home sales fell 2.4% in June to 4.09M SAAR, median price $440,600
summary: US existing home sales declined 2.4% month-over-month in June 2026 to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.09 million units. The median existing home sale price rose 1.8% year-over-year to $440,600, reflecting persistent affordability constraints amid elevated mortgage rates.
key_facts: Existing home sales 4.09M SAAR in June (-2.4% MoM)

headline: US stock futures rise Friday July 24 as markets attempt to stabilize after $800B tech selloff
summary: Dow futures rose ~0.5%, S&P 500 futures gained ~0.2%, and Nasdaq-100 futures edged up ~0.1% on Friday morning as Wall Street tried to recover from Thursday's tech-driven rout in which Magnificent Seven stocks lost ~$800B in market cap on AI spending concerns.
key_facts: Recovery attempt after Thursday $800B M7 loss
New Trump tariffs on 60 economies effective July 24

headline: S&P 500 -1.5%, Nasdaq -2.9%, Dow -1% for week ending July 24 on AI capex fears
summary: US equity indices posted weekly losses for the week ending July 24, with the Nasdaq falling 2.9%, the S&P 500 declining 1.5%, and the Dow losing 1%. The losses were primarily driven by Alphabet and Tesla earnings revealing massive AI capital spending plans that rattled investor confidence.
key_facts: GOOGL fell ~6% after capex hike to $195-205B
TSLA fell 14.5% on EPS miss and FCF concerns

headline: US dollar index (DXY) holds near 101 as rate hike expectations and oil-driven inflation boost greenback
summary: The US dollar index (DXY) held near 101 on July 24, supported by elevated Fed rate hike expectations (34% July, 78% September odds) and oil-price-driven inflation concerns. The dollar has been near its strongest level since February 2026.
key_facts: Oil surge adding to inflation concerns

headline: Energy XLE leads sectors July 23, up 1.77% to $60.25 on Brent crude surge above $100
summary: The Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE) was among the top sector performers on July 23, rising 1.77% to $60.25 as Brent crude surged above $100 per barrel for the first time in months on escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers in the Red Sea.
key_facts: Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers catalyst

headline: Alphabet's cloud backlog swells to $514B, grew $50B+ sequentially in Q2 2026
summary: Alphabet's Google Cloud division reported a contract backlog of $514B as of Q2 2026, representing sequential growth of more than $50B. Approximately half of the backlog is expected to convert to revenue within 24 months, underscoring the long-term revenue visibility of the AI cloud buildout despite near-term capex concerns.
key_facts: Alphabet also expanding third-party capacity as bridge

headline: Tesla Q2 2026: free cash flow -$1.1B on $5.8B quarterly capex; margins under pressure
summary: Tesla's Q2 2026 results revealed free cash flow of negative $1.1B, driven by record quarterly capital expenditure of $5.8B. Gross margins remained under pressure even as revenue beat expectations, with management characterizing 2026 as the company's largest-ever investment period in AI, robotics, and manufacturing.

headline: Tesla Q2 2026 deliveries ~480K supported revenue beat; EV sector growth context
summary: Tesla reported approximately 480,000 vehicle deliveries in Q2 2026, supporting the 26% year-over-year revenue beat. However, the delivery growth was insufficient to offset profit margin pressure, heavy capital spending on AI and robotics, and negative free cash flow that disappointed investors.
key_facts: Strong delivery growth but margin under pressure
AI and robotics investment diluting EPS

headline: Verizon Q2 2026 key metrics: broadband 339K FWA Q1, postpaid adds first positive Q1 in 13 years
summary: Verizon's Q2 2026 earnings featured improving subscriber metrics built on Q1 momentum: 55K postpaid phone net adds (the first positive Q1 in 13 years), 339K FWA broadband adds, and positive EBITDA growth from Frontier integration. Revenue came in slightly below consensus while EPS was in line.
key_facts: Q1 postpaid adds 55K (first positive Q1 in 13 yrs)

headline: Fed faces inflation at 3.7% and oil-driven energy surge as FOMC July 28-29 approaches
summary: With inflation at 3.7% — well above the 2% target — and oil prices now above $98 on Houthi attacks in the Red Sea, the Federal Reserve faces mounting pressure to raise rates at its July 28-29 meeting. Markets price 34% odds of a July hike and 78% for September.

headline: S&P Global US Manufacturing PMI flash 49.5 in July, slipping into contraction
summary: The S&P Global US Manufacturing PMI fell to 49.5 in July 2026, the flash estimate, dipping below the 50-point expansion/contraction threshold. The reading contrasted with the services sector's robust 55.2 reading, highlighting a two-speed US economy with services leading and manufacturing stalling.

headline: AT&T sets broadband net-add record in Q2 2026: 646K total (367K fiber + 279K FWA)
summary: AT&T's Q2 2026 results showed a record combined broadband quarter: 367K fiber net adds and 279K fixed wireless access (FWA) net adds for a combined 646K, the best result across both categories combined in company history. The company also added 1 million Advanced Connectivity customers.
key_facts: 432K postpaid phone net adds vs 338.5K est

headline: Iberdrola to take control of Finnish utility Caruna for $2.3 billion
summary: Spanish utility Iberdrola announced it would acquire control of Finnish electricity distribution company Caruna for approximately $2.3 billion, expanding its European regulated utility footprint in the Nordic region.
key_facts: Expands Iberdrola's Nordic regulated utility presence

headline: Var Energi to buy BlueNord for $1.3B, creating Europe's biggest independent oil and gas firm
summary: Norway's Var Energi announced plans to acquire BlueNord in a $1.3 billion deal, which upon completion would create Europe's largest independent oil and gas company. The deal was announced July 21, 2026.
key_facts: Creates Europe's biggest independent O&G firm

headline: Magnificent Seven erases $797B in single day as AI spending spree rattles Wall Street
summary: The collective Magnificent Seven index fell 4.8% on July 23, erasing $797B in market value as Alphabet and Tesla revealed AI capital spending commitments that alarmed investors focused on return on investment. The selloff raised broader questions about whether the AI infrastructure buildout is reaching unsustainable levels.
key_facts: Biggest single-day M7 drop since April 2025 tariff tantrum

headline: Nikkei 225 falls ~2.5% July 24 as Magnificent Seven rout spreads to Japan
summary: Japan's Nikkei 225 fell approximately 2.5% on July 24 as the Magnificent Seven's $797B selloff spread to Asian technology stocks. Japanese chip and AI-related equities led losses as investors reassessed the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending.

headline: July 24 marks expiration of Trump's Section 122 emergency tariff; new 10-12.5% regime replaces it
summary: July 24, 2026 marked the expiration of President Trump's emergency Section 122 trade act tariffs, which had been put in place as a stopgap after the Supreme Court struck down broader emergency-powers tariffs in February 2026. The new 10-12.5% forced-labor tariff framework now governs US trade policy.
key_facts: Supreme Court struck down emergency-powers tariffs in February 2026
New 10-12.5% forced-labor framework now in effect

headline: July FOMC meeting has no SEP; statement language and Warsh press conference carry full repricing weight
summary: The July 28-29 FOMC meeting will not produce a Summary of Economic Projections, making Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference and the statement language the primary vehicles for any policy signals. Markets see the meeting as a communication event with a live but minority probability of a hike.
key_facts: Statement language is primary policy signal
Kevin Warsh press conference July 29 at 2:30 PM ET
Quarter-point increase is live and tradable

headline: US existing home sales June median price $440,600 (+1.8% YoY) as affordability stays stretched
summary: The median price of existing US home sales reached $440,600 in June 2026, up 1.8% year-over-year, as housing affordability remained under pressure from elevated mortgage rates tied to expectations of further Fed tightening. Existing sales fell 2.4% to a 4.09M seasonally adjusted annual rate.

headline: 2026 IPO activity reaches $28.2B through May in 46 traditional offerings; mega-IPO era cited
summary: Traditional IPO activity through May 2026 totaled $28.2B across 46 deals, more than doubling the $11.1B raised in 25 deals in the same period of 2025. SPAC IPOs have also accelerated to 98 deals raising $17.1B YTD. The pace is being described as the start of a mega-IPO era.
key_facts: 46 traditional IPOs raised $28.2B YTD through May 2026

headline: AT&T maintains FY 2026 guidance: adj EPS $2.25-2.35, FCF at least $18B
summary: Despite Q2 revenue of $31.6B landing modestly below analyst consensus, AT&T maintained its full-year 2026 guidance of adjusted EPS in the $2.25-2.35 range and free cash flow of at least $18 billion. The maintained guidance and strong subscriber results drove the stock up 5% premarket.

headline: NextEra Energy Q2 2026 preview: backlog growth and capex trajectory key checkpoints for NEE
summary: Analysts watching NextEra Energy's Q2 2026 results (reported July 24) focused on renewable energy project backlog growth, capital expenditure deployment, and whether EPS of ~$1.10 could be achieved on estimated revenue of $8.15B (+21.9% YoY). NEE has beaten estimates in each of the last four quarters.
key_facts: Renewable project backlog growth key focus
CEO John Ketchum, CFO Mike Dunne

headline: Iran warns of retaliation against US-linked energy assets as Trump threatens extended strikes
summary: Iran warned it would retaliate against US-linked infrastructure and energy assets across the region in response to President Trump's threat to extend US strikes beyond Iranian military targets. The escalation kept oil prices elevated near $100 per barrel despite Friday morning profit-taking.
key_facts: Iran threatened retaliation against US-linked energy assets
Trump threatened to extend US strikes on Iran
Brent held near $98.82 despite slight pullback

headline: Semiconductor stocks attempt rebound July 24 as AI infrastructure demand thesis remains intact
summary: Semiconductor stocks staged a tentative recovery on July 24 following the prior week's AI-capex selloff, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) attempting to reclaim recent losses. Intel's 18A node is entering high-volume production and attracting customers including Microsoft and Qualcomm, while AMD and Micron remain key AI infrastructure beneficiaries.
key_facts: MU beneficiary of AI memory demand

headline: Alphabet Q2 2026 EPS $9.11 beats; revenue $119.8B (+24%), cloud +82%; shares drop ~6%
summary: Alphabet's Q2 2026 earnings call revealed EPS of $9.11 on revenue of $119.8B (+24% YoY, vs $116.9B consensus). Google Cloud revenue surged 82% to $24.77B and the CFO cited the need to accelerate AI computing capacity as the rationale for raising full-year capex to $195-205B — which drove the stock down ~6%.

headline: US Composite PMI 54.6 in July consistent with 2.3% annualized GDP growth at Q3 start
summary: The S&P Global US Composite PMI rose to 54.6 in July 2026 from 52.9, its highest reading in months, consistent with an annualized GDP expansion rate of approximately 2.3%. The reading signals that despite manufacturing contraction (49.5), the broader US economy maintained solid momentum at the start of Q3.
